additionalProperty.name: Canonical Language
additionalProperty.value: English Canonical Definition Tax-Relevant Event Boundary Standard (TREBS) governs how a sufficiently formed real-world, economic, operational, transactional, digital, autonomous, machine-generated, or value-affecting event is bounded as a distinct governed event by establishing what belongs within its governed extent, what remains outside it, where separation from adjacent or overlapping activity is required, and when an established Event Boundary must be reconsidered or revised. TREBS receives a Governed Formed Event from the Tax-Relevant Event Formation Standard (TREFS) and establishes the governed boundary necessary for that event to proceed through subsequent TREGA™ lifecycle stages without allowing Event Boundary governance to determine Event Timing, Event Location, Event Participation, Event-to-Value Association, Event Relationships, legal taxability, Tax Jurisdiction, taxpayer status, tax liability, or jurisdiction-specific tax consequences.

additionalProperty.name: Canonical Language
additionalProperty.value: English Canonical Definition Tax-Relevant Event Formation Standard (TREFS) governs how a sufficiently recognized real-world, economic, operational, transactional, digital, autonomous, machine-generated, or value-affecting occurrence is transformed into a coherent governed event structure capable of progressing through the subsequent stages of the TREGA™ lifecycle. TREFS establishes the governance conditions through which recognized occurrence elements are structurally organized into an Event Formation, including the identification of materially relevant formation components, their assembly, material formation dependencies, operational root association, and the integrity of the resulting formation.

additionalProperty.name: Canonical Language
additionalProperty.value: UCL — Universal Canonical Language Canonical Definition The Tax-Relevant Event Participation Standard (TREPS) governs how human, organizational, digital, machine, autonomous, infrastructural, and other materially relevant actors are represented as participants in a spatially and temporally governed Tax-Relevant Event. TREPS establishes the governance conditions under which an actor may legitimately be associated with the event, distinguished from other actors, represented according to its operational participation, and maintained as part of the governed event representation. TREPS governs participation in the event. It does not determine whether a participant is legally a taxpayer, taxable person, liable party, beneficial owner, permanent establishment, tax representative, withholding agent, employer, employee, supplier, customer, or any other jurisdiction-specific legal or tax status.

@graph.description: OOF™ Tax-Relevant Event Timing Standard - (TRETS). Tax-Relevant Event Timing Standard - (TRETS) OOF™ Origin Open Foundation™ Independent Methodological.

additionalProperty.name: Canonical Language
additionalProperty.value: English ------------------------------ Canonical Definition The Tax-Relevant Event Timing Standard (TRETS) governs how a sufficiently bounded real-world, economic, operational, transactional, digital, autonomous, machine-generated, or value-affecting event is temporally situated through governed identification of its operational time, start, completion, duration, and temporal order. TRETS establishes the governance conditions through which a Governed Bounded Event becomes a Governed Temporally Situated Event capable of progressing through subsequent TREGA™ lifecycle stages. It governs the temporal representation of what happened operationally without determining the legal tax point, tax period, filing period, recognition date under tax law, legal timing of tax liability, or any other jurisdiction-specific taxation consequence.

@graph.name: OOF™ Tax-Relevant Value Association Standard - (TRVAS)
@graph.description: OOF™ Tax-Relevant Value Association Standard - (TRVAS). Tax-Relevant Value Association Standard - (TRVAS) OOF™ Origin Open Foundation™ Independent.

additionalProperty.name: Canonical Language
additionalProperty.value: UCL — Universal Canonical Language Canonical Definition The Tax-Relevant Value Association Standard (TRVAS) governs how value references, value states, value changes, and other governed value results are associated with a Governed Participatory Event so that the event can carry a sufficiently structured representation of value into subsequent Tax-Relevant Event governance. TRVAS establishes which governed value information legitimately belongs to the event, how that relationship is represented, how multiple value associations are distinguished, how value states and changes are connected to the event, and how those associations remain traceable. TRVAS does not determine the origin, emergence, development, degradation, nullification, restoration, extinction, ownership, economic meaning, or complete lifecycle of value. Those questions belong to VFM® — Value Flow Mechanism and other appropriate governance architectures. TRVAS also does not determine taxable value, Tax Base, consideration under law, customs value, transfer-pricing value, market value under a jurisdiction-specific rule, deductible amount, taxable income, taxable gain, tax rate, or Tax Liability.
